author: kirubaharan181
description: Use when assessing a business case: strategy, discovery, estimates, approval. Do NOT use for detailed requirements or sprint planning.
purpose: Turns a business problem into a validated, costed and approved opportunity so engineering effort starts on something worth building. It owns stages 1-10: strategy, market research, client engagement, discovery, analysis, planning, feasibility, budget, approval and contract compliance.
when_to_use: A new product, feature or client request needs a business case before requirements are written.
A funding, go or no-go, or contract decision needs evidence.
Market, feasibility or budget assumptions need to be tested.
when_not_to_use: Writing testable requirements or designs: use requirements-design.
Planning sprints or tracking delivery: use project-agile-management.
Choosing technology or system structure: use technical-architecture.
prerequisites: A stated problem, opportunity or client request and a named sponsor.
Access to existing strategy, market, cost and contract documents the team may use.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: business case with measurable goals and a do-nothing option
market and feasibility findings with sources
approval record naming the human approver and conditions

decision_rules.action: Stop and ask for one; do not approve a case that cannot be measured.
Convert it to a range with assumptions before it is used for approval.
Record it in the obligations register and route to the compliance owner.

decision_rules.situation: Approver is not a named human
decision_rules.action: Mark the decision NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL; never record an agent as approver.

quality_gates: Goals have measures, baselines and dates
Every market or cost claim cites a source or is labelled an assumption
A named human approved funding, with conditions recorded

examples.title: Assess a new feature request
examples.request: A client asks for a self-service invoice portal. Should we build it?
examples.context: Support spends 30 percent of its time on invoice requests; no portal exists.
examples.behavior: Measure the current support load, list options including do-nothing and a cheaper export feature, estimate each as a range, and recommend one with risks.
examples.output: Business case with baseline (support hours per month), three options, estimate ranges and a recommendation awaiting sponsor approval.
examples.acceptance: Each option has a cost range and an expected change in the baseline measure.

examples.title: Check contract obligations before approval
examples.request: Review the draft statement of work for obligations that affect delivery.
examples.context: The contract requires data to stay in one country and 24-hour breach notice.
examples.behavior: List each obligation as what, owner and evidence, flag any the team cannot meet, and send gaps to legal.
examples.output: Obligations register with owners and a list of unmet obligations.
examples.acceptance: No obligation lacks an owner; gaps are raised before approval.

limitations: Cannot verify market data it is given; sources must be cited by the user or found with approved tools.
Does not decide funding: a named human approves.
Estimates are ranges from stated assumptions, not commitments.

troubleshooting.resolution: Ask who funds and accepts the outcome; do not proceed to approval without a name.
Record both with dates and methods, use the more conservative figure, and flag the conflict.
Use a labelled assumption and schedule a re-estimate at the first checkpoint.

handoffs.artifact: approved business case, goals, scope and constraints
approved project charter inputs and budget
